## Text analytics: Sparse vectors

**TF-IDF:**

Explain how $idf_i$ changes:

- when $\frac{N}{df_i}$ gets smaller and approaches 1, the log approaches 0 and the $tf_{ij}$ will have low weights in the TF-IDF
- if the term is very rare, the $\frac{N}{df_i}$ gets large and the terms will have more weight in the TF-IDF (at teh same time, `log` ensures that outliers/very rare terms do not have an excessive influence on TF-IDF)

**Example with a mini corpus after preprocessing**

<div class="smaller">

| Document | Tokens |
|---|---|
| D1 | `jupiter largest gas planet` |
| D2 | `saturn gas planet rings` |
| D3 | `mars rocky planet` |

</div>

<br>

Vocabulary:

<div style="font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.75em;">
[gas, jupiter, largest, mars, planet, rings, rocky, saturn]
</div>

<br>

Sparse vector for **D1**:

<div style="
display: grid;
grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 1fr);
gap: 0.35em;
font-family: monospace;
font-size: 0.7em;
text-align: center;
">

<div>gas</div>
<div>jupiter</div>
<div>largest</div>
<div>mars</div>
<div>planet</div>
<div>rings</div>
<div>rocky</div>
<div>saturn</div>

<div style="background:#cfe8d6; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">1</div>
<div style="background:#cfe8d6; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">1</div>
<div style="background:#cfe8d6; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">1</div>
<div style="background:#eeeeee; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">0</div>
<div style="background:#cfe8d6; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">1</div>
<div style="background:#eeeeee; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">0</div>
<div style="background:#eeeeee; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">0</div>
<div style="background:#eeeeee; padding:0.35em; border-radius:6px;">0</div>

</div>

<br>

<div class="smaller">

| Representation | Vector for D1 |
|---|---|
| Binary occurrence | `[1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0]` |
| Term occurrence | `[1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0]` |
| Term frequency | `[.25, .25, .25, 0, .25, 0, 0, 0]` |
| TF-IDF | `[.18, .48, .48, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]` |

</div>

Note: using $log_{10}$ for ease of calculation (libraries often use the natural $log_2$).

- $w_{Gas;D1} = 1\times log(\frac{3}{2}) = 0.18$
- $w_{Jupyter;D1} = 1\times log(\frac{3}{1}) = 0.48$
- $w_{largest;D1} = 1\times log(\frac{3}{1}) = 0.48$
- $w_{Planet;D1} = 1\times log(\frac{3}{3}) = 0$

Note: `Planet` has $idf=0$ and will be eliminated from TF-IDF.

Most entries are zero because each document only uses a small part of the full vocabulary.

## Dense representations

Highlight that dense representations allow us to determine semantic similarity based on mathematical operations.
